clue.text: Uncle's business is selling fizzy drinks

definitions.meaning: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, and to pop something is to pawn it, so his premises are a pawn establishment
pop is fizzy soft drink, so a store for it is a pop retailer

explanation.surface: A relative runs a little business flogging soft drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker; 'pop' is British slang for pawning something, as in 'Pop goes the weasel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker's premises was called a pop shop, and the phrase read literally is a store dealing in soda.

clue.text: Humiliating criticism gets recorded

definitions.meaning: a snub or crushing remark that belittles someone
written down, entered in a record

explanation.surface: A cutting remark gets caught on tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting snub is a put-down, and to put something down on paper is to note it in writing.

clue.text: A heart-throb full of beans, maybe

definitions.meaning: a single beat of the heart felt at the wrist
beans, lentils and peas are edible seeds of the legume family

explanation.surface: A dreamy idol who is bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-throb' wants to be a pin-up; here it is one beat of the heart. 'Full of beans' looks like the idiom for lively, but the beans are an example of the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb of the heart is felt as a beat at the wrist, and legume seeds such as lentils are called by the same name.

clue.text: Marx used to talk endlessly — endlessly

indicators.note: the second endlessly tells us to cut the final letter off the phrase just found

parts.note: to harp on is to keep talking about the same thing without stopping

explanation.surface: A complaint that Marx never stopped going on about things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' appears twice: the first belongs to the phrase HARP ON (keep talking), the second removes its last letter. The joke is that this Marx brother famously never spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Harpo was the silent harp-playing brother of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: Cautious punter roughly hugged daughter

indicators.note: hugged means one piece is held inside the shuffled letters of the other
roughly suggests the letters of the word punter are approximated, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A careful gambler gave his girl a rough hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges the gambler's word into PRUENT, and 'hugged' sets D inside it after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wary and sensible acts with prudence, avoiding risks.

clue.text: Not the fare for noblemen

parts.note: read as a menu remark it suggests plain food unfit for lords; read politically it is the lower chamber, not the house where peers sit

explanation.surface: A snooty verdict that this food is beneath the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: The lower house of the UK Parliament is for elected members, not peers, while the word also means shared rations, as served in a college hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means daily food rations shared at a common table, and it also names the elected chamber that excludes peers.

clue.text: Fellow cleric heard to demand a painkiller

indicators.note: heard signals that we want a word which sounds like the clue phrase rather than its spelling

parts.note: a co-dean would be a fellow dean, a senior cleric sharing the post

explanation.surface: A churchman's colleague asks for something to ease the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow cleric' is CO-DEAN, which said aloud matches the drug's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate drug used to relieve mild to moderate pain.

clue.text: Was effective in brewing mild tea without it

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece
brewing means the letters of mild tea are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Making a weak cuppa without the usual ingredient still did the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' turns MILD TEA into MILATED, and 'without' (outside) puts that around IT after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To militate is to have weight or influence for or against an outcome.

clue.text: Arrangement for many a catalogue customer

definitions.text: Arrangement for many a catalogue customer

parts.note: order is a tidy arrangement or sequence
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many

explanation.surface: A setup that suits lots of mail-order shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the thing: a printed sheet that many catalogue shoppers fill in to buy goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail-order shoppers fill in a printed sheet listing the goods they want to buy.

clue.text: Thronged to see me covered in grass

indicators.note: covered in means one piece is wrapped inside the other, so the grass word goes around

parts.note: sward is an expanse of short grass, a lawn or turf

explanation.surface: People crowded in to look at me lying in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm is to crowd together in large numbers, as bees do.

clue.text: Skirt the issue to gain agreement

definitions.meaning: to speak around a subject without tackling it directly
to win someone over by persuasion

explanation.surface: Dodging the main point as a way of winning people over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to avoid a topic by discussing its edges and to persuade someone until they concur.

clue.text: She broadcast daily

indicators.note: broadcast in its old sense of scattered widely, so the letters of daily are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman who goes on air every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a woman can be called by it.

clue.text: Tedious poet begging a flower to bloom?

parts.note: ope is a poetic, archaic form meaning to open, as a bud does
a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A dull poet pleading with a blossom to open up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poet begging' sets the scene: a poet would say 'Ope, rose!', using the archaic word for open, as a plea to a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Operose is a literary word for laborious or wearisome, needing much effort.

clue.text: Bury decapitated man in the meantime

parts.note: to inter someone is to bury them

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, that is the first letter, comes off the name

parts.note: Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: A grisly instruction to bury a headless corpse for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' removes the first letter from TIM, a man's name, leaving IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes the stopgap period between two events, meaning provisionally or meanwhile.

clue.text: Novel fortified building for this city

parts.note: novel means new, fresh
a castle is a fortified building

explanation.surface: A book titled after a stronghold is set in a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but means fresh. The city is in north-east England, named for its Norman fort.
explanation.definitionFit: A major city on the Tyne in north-east England.

clue.text: Courted after having downed tools

definitions.meaning: dated as a couple, an old-fashioned way of saying went out together
went on strike, left work in protest

explanation.surface: Romance began once the workers stopped for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walked out' was old British usage for a couple going steady; 'downed tools' means struck, the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Courting couples were once said to walk out together, and strikers leave the workplace in protest.

clue.text: Temperate Tibetans dispersed around noon

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the other piece
dispersed means the letters of Tibetans are scattered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Sober folk from Tibet scattered around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' turns TIBETANS into ABSTIENT, and 'around' puts it round N after the sixth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone temperate refrains from drink or indulgence, keeping self-denial.

clue.text: Walked around a region of Asia Minor

indicators.note: around means the walking word wraps round the single letter

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, to walk

explanation.surface: A traveller describes strolling about Anatolia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Troad is the ancient district in north-west Anatolia where Troy stood.

clue.text: Consequently taken back to Aegean island

indicators.note: taken back here means the combined pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: so means therefore, consequently
led means taken somewhere, guided

explanation.surface: A traveller is therefore escorted back to a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the two pieces read together. Delos is the small sacred island of the Cyclades.
explanation.definitionFit: Delos is a small Greek island in the Cyclades, sacred birthplace of Apollo.

clue.text: Try desperately to fit dado below the entrance

indicators.note: below in a down clue means the second piece comes under the first

parts.note: a door is an entrance
the dado is the die, the plain middle block of a pedestal

explanation.surface: A decorator struggles to fix a wall panel under the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dado' looks like a wall rail but is the architectural term for the die of a pedestal.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate all-or-nothing effort is described with this phrase, meaning succeed or perish.

clue.text: Retired medic shoots fellow commissioner

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the medic abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: MO is medical officer, a doctor
buds are new shoots on a plant
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: An ex-doctor guns down a colleague on the committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' reverses the doctor's abbreviation. 'shoots' wants to be a verb of firing but is a noun for new growth.
explanation.definitionFit: An official appointed to investigate public complaints against institutions is a kind of commissioner.

clue.text: Finished on time despite being past it

parts.note: over means ended, finished
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Arriving punctually even though too old for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beyond the permitted years makes someone too old, so no longer up to it.

clue.text: Public-transport supremo performing in public

parts.note: a bus is public transport
a king is a supreme ruler

explanation.surface: A transport chief entertains passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Street entertainers play music or perform for passers-by in exchange for coins.

clue.text: Has arrived, but clearly can't be found!

definitions.meaning: split into two words it says present at this moment, at this place

explanation.surface: Someone has turned up, yet is plainly missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters split as NOW HERE mean present, and run together mean in no place, which is the paradox the exclamation enjoys.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in no place, while divided after the third letter it says present at this moment.

clue.text: Former head of English entered punctually

indicators.note: entered means the first letter is put inside the phrase for punctually

parts.note: on time means punctually

indicators.note: head of picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A past leader of the English department arrived exactly on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes E from English, and 'entered' sets it inside the phrase for punctually, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from an earlier period, a previous holder of a role, is a former one.

clue.text: A bird to gulp down food

definitions.meaning: to take food down the throat

explanation.surface: A bird bolting its meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The fork-tailed migrant songbird shares its name with the act of taking food down the throat.

clue.text: Old German queen has to make adjustments

parts.note: alt is German for old
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: An elderly German monarch has to change things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old German' is not an ancient person but the German word for old. ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change or modify it.

clue.text: Admitted having left school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil confessed to having dropped out of school.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is an elite English private boarding school near Windsor. 'Admitted' is confessed, revealed, not let in.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is an idiom for revealing or confessing something secret.

clue.text: Ran a car into the crowd

definitions.meaning: steered a motor vehicle, in the past tense
a herd or throng of moving animals or people

explanation.surface: Someone motored straight into a mass of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The past of drive means steered a car, and a moving herd or throng is also called by this word.

clue.text: Old philosopher enables vulgar peer to let rip

parts.note: aristo is informal, slangy shortening for an aristocrat, a peer

indicators.note: let rip means set loose, so the letters of let are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A coarse lord lets fly at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rip' turns LET into TLE; 'vulgar' marks the slang shortening of aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek thinker who tutored Alexander the Great and studied under Plato.

clue.text: Qualify in French with credit

parts.note: en is French for in
a title is a credit, as in screen credits or a claim to something

explanation.surface: Earning a qualification in French gives a sense of achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a right or claim to something makes them eligible.

clue.text: Ignored botch-up by French department

indicators.note: a botch-up is a muddle, so the letters of Ignored are jumbled

explanation.surface: A French local authority overlooked a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gironde is an administrative area of south-west France around Bordeaux.
